1	﻿# Project Manifest – Starfield Load Order Keeper
     2	
     3	> Source-of-truth overview for future AI agents. Do not infer behavior beyond what is documented here.
     4	
     5	---
     6	
     7	## Domain Context
     8	
     9	Starfield uses a line-based text file called `Plugins.txt` to define which mods load and in what order. Once a save game exists, the order of existing lines must not change — internal object references depend on it (e.g., equipped items added by mods). Both the game itself and mod manager tools frequently rearrange the file, which can corrupt save games. This application monitors `Plugins.txt`, detects unauthorized changes, and restores the correct load order while safely appending new mods.
    10	
    11	---
    12	
    13	## Navigation
    14	
    15	This manifest is split into logical sections for easier maintenance:
    16	
    17	### Core Documentation
    18	
    19	1. **[Tech Stack & Patterns](tech-stack.md)** - Runtime, libraries, frameworks, and architectural patterns
    20	2. **[File Tree](file-tree.md)** - Logical overview of project structure
    21	3. **[Data Flows](data-flows.md)** - Key application workflows and coordinator interactions
    22	4. **[Constraints & Invariants](constraints.md)** - Rules, guarantees, and system constraints
    23	5. **[Localization](localization.md)** - Zero-hardcoding localization architecture and translation guidelines
    24	6. **[File Formats & Handling](file-formats.md)** - Encoding rules, file format specs, and I/O conventions
    25	7. **[UI Design System](ui-design.md)** - Visual design conventions, component taxonomy, and interaction patterns
    26	
    27	### API Reference
    28	
    29	8. **[API Surface](api-surface.md)** - Public signatures for all coordinators, models, services, ViewModels, views, and converters
    30	
    31	---
    32	
    33	## Quick Reference
    34	
    35	- **Target Framework**: .NET 9
    36	- **UI Framework**: WPF with MaterialDesign v5
    37	- **Architecture**: MVVM + Coordinator Pattern + Instance Services
    38	- **Localization**: See **[Localization Guide](localization.md)** for complete documentation
    39	  - **Locale Codes**: en-US, de-DE, fr-FR, es-ES, it-IT, zh-CN, ja-JP, pt-BR
    40	  - **Zero-Hardcoding**: New languages require only JSON file (no code changes)
    41	- **Key Coordinators**: FileMonitoring, Status, UpdateCheck, Profile, Configuration, GameLauncher, WindowManager
    42	- **Static Services**: Settings, File, Profile, Diff, ReferenceHistory, UpdateCheck, Version, DateTimeFormatting, ErrorLogging, DebugState
    43	- **Instance Services**: FileOperations, ReferenceManagement, WindowLifecycle, ViewModelInitializer
    44	- **Localization Services**: LocalizationService (singleton), LocalizationJsonNormalizer
    45	- **Helper Classes**: CoordinatorEventBinder, MenuViewModel, LanguageOption
    46	- **Text ViewModels**: Per-window text ViewModels in `ViewTexts/`; see `tech-stack.md` for the full list
    47	
    48

1	﻿# Localization Architecture
     2	
     3	> Comprehensive guide to the zero-hardcoding localization system
     4	
     5	---
     6	
     7	## Table of Contents
     8	
     9	1. [Zero-Hardcoding Design](#zero-hardcoding-design)
    10	2. [Plural Forms — CountFormat / CountSingular Pattern](#plural-forms--countformat--countsingular-pattern)
    11	3. [Chinese and Japanese Translation Guidelines](#chinese-and-japanese-translation-guidelines)
    12	4. [Locale File Structure](#locale-file-structure)
    13	5. [Language Preference System](#language-preference-system)
    14	6. [Adding a New Language](#adding-a-new-language)
    15	7. [Testing LocalizationService](#testing-localizationservice)
    16	
    17	---
    18	
    19	## Zero-Hardcoding Design
    20	
    21	The localization system uses a **zero-hardcoding architecture** where adding a new language requires **only a JSON file**:
    22	
    23	```json
    24	{
    25	  "LocaleName": "Português (Brasil)",
    26	  "ParentCulture": "pt",
    27	  "MainWindow": { "key": "translated value" },
    28	  "Settings": { "key": "translated value" }
    29	}
    30	```
    31	
    32	No C# code changes, no compilation, no hardcoded mappings. The system automatically:
    33	- Discovers new locale files via file system scanning
    34	- Reads display names from `LocaleName` property
    35	- Maps parent cultures via `ParentCulture` property
    36	- Populates language dropdown dynamically
    37	- Supports automatic system locale detection
    38	
    39	### Supported Languages
    40	
    41	- **Total Languages**: 8
    42	- **Locale Codes**: en-US, de-DE, fr-FR, es-ES, it-IT, zh-CN, ja-JP, pt-BR
    43	- **Total Strings**: See `en-US.json` for the current key count (use it as the translation template) 
    44	- **User-Selectable**: Language preference dropdown in Settings
    45	- **Auto-Detection**: Automatic system locale detection
    46	- **Extensibility**: New languages require only JSON file (no code changes)
    47	
    48	---
    49	
    50	## Plural Forms — CountFormat / CountSingular Pattern
    51	
    52	Several DiffDialog strings describe counts of mods affected by a load-order change. These use a **paired key convention** to handle the singular/plural distinction without runtime branching in the JSON keys:
    53	
    54	| Key suffix | When used | Example value |
    55	|------------|-----------|---------------|
    56	| `CountFormat` | Count is **2 or more** — contains `{0}` placeholder | `"{0} mod(s) removed"` |
    57	| `CountSingular` | Count is **exactly 1** — no `{0}` placeholder | `"1 mod removed"` |
    58	
    59	### Contract
    60

1	# Tech Stack & Patterns
     2	
     3	> Detailed overview of runtime, libraries, frameworks, and architectural patterns used in the application.
     4	
     5	---
     6	
     7	## Runtime / Platform
     8	
     9	- .NET 9
    10	- WPF desktop application
    11	- **Localization**: JSON-based, zero-hardcoding architecture
    12	  - Supported locales: en-US, de-DE, fr-FR, es-ES, it-IT, zh-CN, ja-JP, pt-BR
    13	  - Automatic system language detection with fallback
    14	  - Runtime culture switching support
    15	
    16	---
    17	
    18	## Libraries / Frameworks
    19	
    20	- **CommunityToolkit.Mvvm**
    21	  - `ObservableObject`, `[ObservableProperty]`, `[RelayCommand]`, `RelayCommand`, `AsyncRelayCommand`, `IRelayCommand`, `IAsyncRelayCommand`
    22	- **MaterialDesignThemes** / **MaterialDesignColors** for dialogs, icons, and card layouts (v5)
    23	- **SteamLibraryVdfParser** internal helper for Steam `libraryfolders.vdf` parsing using standard .NET APIs only
    24	- **System.Text.Json** for JSON serialization/deserialization (localization files, configuration, metadata)
    25	- **System.Text.Encodings.Web** for JSON Unicode handling in localization
    26	- Standard .NET `System.*` APIs for I/O, processes, collections, and globalization
    27	
    28	---
    29	
    30	## Architectural Patterns
    31	
    32	### MVVM
    33	
    34	**ViewModels:**
    35	- `MainViewModel`, `SettingsViewModel`, `DiffDialogViewModel`, `SwitchProfileViewModel`, `ManageProfilesViewModel`, `ProfilePropertiesViewModel`, `ConfirmationDialogViewModel`, `AboutViewModel`, `UpdateOptionsViewModel`, `ReferenceHistoryViewModel`, `CommentInputViewModel`, `ViewPendingChangesViewModel`, `ErrorDialogViewModel`
    36	
    37	**Text ViewModels (Localization):**
    38	- `MenuViewModel`, `MainWindowTexts`, `MainWindowStatusTexts`, `AboutViewModel`, `ErrorDialogTexts`, `CommentInputTexts`, `ConfirmationDialogTexts`, `ConfigInvalidOverlayTexts`, `SettingsWindowTexts`, `DiffDialogTexts`, `ManageProfilesTexts`, `ProfilePropertiesTexts`, `SwitchProfileTexts`, `ReferenceHistoryTexts`, `ReferenceManagementStatusTexts`, `UpdateOptionsTexts`, `ViewPendingChangesTexts`, `ViewModelInitializerStatusTexts`, `CommonTexts`
    39	
    40	**Views:**
    41	- `MainWindow`, `SettingsWindow`, `DiffWindow`, `SwitchProfileWindow`, `ManageProfilesWindow`, `ProfilePropertiesWindow`, `ConfirmationDialog`, `AboutWindow`, `UpdateOptionsDialog`, `ReferenceHistoryWindow`, `CommentInputDialog`, `ViewPendingChangesWindow`, `ErrorDialog`
    42	
    43	**User Controls:**
    44	- `ConfigInvalidOverlay`
    45	
    46	### Coordinator Pattern
    47	
    48	Coordinators handle specific domain logic and state management:
    49	
    50	- All coordinators inherit from `CoordinatorBase` (provides `INotifyPropertyChanged` + `IDisposable`)
    51	- Event-driven communication between coordinators and ViewModels
    52	- **Coordinators:**
    53	  - `FileMonitoringCoordinator`: Periodic file monitoring, change detection, Steam process detection, sorting recommendations
    54	  - `StatusCoordinator`: Status message management and history tracking
    55	  - `UpdateCheckCoordinator`: Background and manual update checking with caching
    56	  - `ProfileCoordinator`: Active profile state management and switching
    57	  - `ConfigurationCoordinator`: Configuration validation with caching and detailed error reporting
    58	  - `GameLauncherCoordinator`: SFSE detection and game launching
    59	  - `WindowManager`: Window lifecycle management and duplicate prevention
    60	
    61	### Static Services
    62	
    63	- `SettingsService`: configuration persistence and default path discovery (includes Steam library detection)
    64	- `FileService`: plugins/reference file operations plus diff helpers
    65	- `DiffService`: LCS-based diff pipeline — computes the longest common subsequence of mod lists, classifies changes (Removed, Moved, Replaced, Inserted, Added), groups dependent shifts under their causal change, and constructs localized `DiffLineModel` entries for the UI
    66	- `ProfileService`: profile discovery, CRUD, switching, and file scaffolding
    67	- `VersionService`: centralized application version retrieval
    68	- `UpdateCheckService`: GitHub API integration for version checking with caching
    69	- `ReferenceHistoryService`: version history management, archiving, rollback, and pending changes tracking
    70	- `DateTimeFormattingService`: user-friendly date/time formatting utilities
    71	- `ErrorLoggingService`: exception logging with user privacy protection (path sanitization)
    72	- `DebugStateService`: application state capture for debugging with sanitized paths
    73	
    74	### Localization Services
    75	
    76	- `LocalizationService`: singleton service managing JSON-based translations
    77	  - Thread-safe string retrieval with culture-specific lookups
    78	  - Format string support with placeholder replacement
    79	  - Runtime culture switching with event notification
    80	  - Automatic system locale detection with parent culture mapping

1	# UI Design System
     2	
     3	> Visual design conventions, component taxonomy, and interaction patterns.
     4	
     5	---
     6	
     7	## Theme
     8	
     9	- **Material Design v5** with dark mode by default.
    10	- **Primary color**: Lime. **Secondary color**: LightGreen.
    11	- Semantic color brushes for theme consistency — never hardcoded hex values.
    12	- Elevated surfaces with shadows for depth.
    13	- Rounded corners (8px) for modern aesthetic.
    14	- All UI text must use data bindings (no hardcoded strings in XAML) to support localization.
    15	
    16	---
    17	
    18	## Button Taxonomy
    19	
    20	| Type | Style | Use Case | Examples |
    21	|------|-------|----------|----------|
    22	| **Raised** | Elevated, filled | Primary actions | Save, Create, Update, Fix Load Order |
    23	| **Outlined** | Border, no fill | Secondary actions | Cancel, Browse, Close |
    24	| **Flat** | No border or elevation | Tertiary / inline actions | Auto-detected path links |
    25	
    26	### Label Conventions
    27	
    28	- **Ellipsis suffix** (`...`): indicates a dialog or additional interaction will follow (e.g., "Save...", "Browse...", "Download options...").
    29	- **Action verbs**: prefer specific verbs ("Delete Profile", "Fix Load Order") over generic labels ("OK", "Apply").
    30	
    31	---
    32	
    33	## Confirmation Dialogs
    34	
    35	All confirmations use `ConfirmationDialog` (custom Material Design v5 control) — never `MessageBox`.
    36	
    37	### Icon Types
    38	
    39	| Icon | Color | Use Case |
    40	|------|-------|----------|
    41	| Information | Blue | Neutral notifications |
    42	| Question | Purple | User decisions |
    43	| Warning | Orange | Destructive or risky actions |
    44	| Error | Red | Failures and critical problems |
    45	
    46	### Destructive Action Pattern
    47	
    48	- Warning icon with detailed impact summary (bullet-point list of changes).
    49	- Default button set to "No" for safety.
    50	- Action cannot be undone clearly stated.
    51	
    52	---
    53	
    54	## Status Indicators
    55	
    56	### Color Coding
    57	
    58	| Type | Color | Brush |
    59	|------|-------|-------|
    60	| Info | Blue | Primary |
    61	| Success | Green | Tertiary |
    62	| Warning | Orange | Secondary |
    63	| Error | Red | Error |
    64	
    65	### XAML Brush Names
    66	
    67	- Error: `{DynamicResource MaterialDesign.Brush.Error}`
    68	- Success: `{DynamicResource MaterialDesign.Brush.Tertiary}`
    69	- Info: `{DynamicResource MaterialDesign.Brush.Primary}`
    70	- Warning: `{DynamicResource MaterialDesign.Brush.Secondary}`
    71	
    72	Always use semantic brushes — never hardcoded hex values. Prefer colored foreground text over colored backgrounds for status messages.
    73	
    74	### Diff Window Brush Resources (`Styles/DiffBrushes.xaml`)
    75	
    76	All diff change type colors are defined as semantic brush resources and referenced via `{DynamicResource}` in `DiffWindow.xaml`.
    77	
    78	| Brush Key | Hex Color | Used For |
    79	|-----------|-----------|----------|
    80	| `DiffBrush.Added` | `#1A4CAF50` | Added mod row background |
    81	| `DiffBrush.Removed` | `#1AF44336` | Removed mod row background |
    82	| `DiffBrush.Inserted` | `#1AFFEB3B` | Inserted mod row background |
    83	| `DiffBrush.Moved` | `#1A2196F3` | Moved mod row background |
    84	| `DiffBrush.Replaced` | `#1A9C27B0` | Replaced mod row background |
    85	| `DiffBrush.Context` | `#08FFFFFF` | Unchanged context line row background |
    86	| `DiffBrush.SortingBannerBackground` | `#FFFFA726` | Sorting recommendation banner background |
    87	| `DiffBrush.SortingBannerBorder` | `#FFFF9800` | Sorting banner border |
    88	
    89	### Diff Window Context Lines and Separators
    90	
    91	- **Default view**: The list shows only changed entries (`Added`, `Removed`, `Moved`, `Replaced`, `Inserted`) to reduce visual noise.
    92	- **Show all mods toggle**: A `MaterialDesignCheckBox` between description and list toggles full-context mode.
    93	- **Context lines** (`DiffChangeType.Unchanged`): Hidden by default; shown in full-context mode with 3% background opacity (`DiffBrush.Context`) and text opacity 0.45. Display 1 unchanged neighbor above and below each change group for spatial orientation. Not selectable (no context menu).
    94	- **Separator** (`DiffChangeType.Separator`): Hidden by default; shown in full-context mode as centered `···` text at 35% opacity between non-adjacent context groups. Transparent background. Not hit-test visible.
    95	
    96	### Main Window Banners
    97	
    98	Banners stack vertically when multiple are active:
    99	
   100	1. **Configuration error** — non-dismissable red banner with "Open settings" button.
   101	2. **Update available** — info bar with "Download options..." button; dismissable for current session.
   102	3. **Steam warning** — orange banner with tooltip; auto-dismisses when Steam closes.
   103	
   104	### Settings Window
   105	
   106	- Permanent status banner — green (valid) or red (specific error message). Updates in real-time on field changes.
   107	
   108	### Change Badge
   109	
   110	- "Manage load order" button text appends `(X changes)` when primary changes are present.
   111	- When dependent changes also exist: appends `(X changes, +Y affected)` where X is the primary count and Y is the dependent count.
   112	- `FileMonitoringCoordinator.ChangeCount` counts primary changes only (excludes `Unchanged` and `Separator` items).
   113	- `FileMonitoringCoordinator.DependentChangeCount` counts all dependent position shifts.
   114	
   115	---
   116	
   117	## Window Types
   118	
   119	### Modal Windows
   120
